strings.Back to the template list, or from the l: Back to the template list, or from the list back to the trigger
strings.Pick a template to edit it. The arrows c: Pick a template to edit it. The arrows change the order in the file; a Library template is a set of loops other templates use, without <Init>.
strings.A Library template has no <Init>: its lo: A Library template has no <Init>: its loops are building blocks for other templates. Each loop lists its variables in <Using>.
strings.The template's <Init>. Each loop lists t: The template's <Init>. Each loop lists the variables it reads in <Using>.
strings.Add to / remove from the selection: Add to / remove from the selection
strings.Move / Rotate / Scale / Rect / Brush too: Move / Rotate / Scale / Rect / Brush tool
strings.Move / rotate / scale with the pointer (: Move / rotate / scale with the pointer (click confirms, right click or Esc cancels)
strings.Lock G / R / S to an axis: Lock G / R / S to an axis
strings.Order in Layer (brush size with the Brus: Order in Layer (brush size with the Brush)
strings.Duplicate (while dragging or G / R / S:: Duplicate (while dragging or G / R / S: keep moving the copies)
strings.Duplicate and drag (keep Alt held to sta: Duplicate and drag (keep Alt held to stamp more)
strings.Play level / Play in Hunter Mode: Play level / Play in Hunter Mode
strings.Everything you make lives in a project:: Everything you make lives in a project: its levels, textures, objects and settings, kept apart from the game's own files. You can have as many projects as you like, and this window is where you pick one.
strings.Let's make your first project. Click the: Let's make your first project. Click the + button (Add Project) and give it any name you like.
strings.Here it is. Click {0} in the list to sel: Here it is. Click {0} in the list to select it.
On the right are the project's details. Click the picture to give the project a thumbnail, and change its name, author or description whenever you like.
strings.Click Open Selected Project to start wor: Click Open Selected Project to start working on it.
strings.This is the Project Manager: everything: This is the Project Manager: everything in your project, sorted into categories. Each one has its own tab on the left. Let's go through them.
strings.Levels are the stages you play, grouped: Levels are the stages you play, grouped by location and by mode (Story or Hunter). Click DOWNTOWN_STORY_01 in the list.
strings.The right side shows the selected level:: The right side shows the selected level: its thumbnail, the name shown in the game, its location and its track settings. You can change them here at any time.
strings.Edit Level opens the selected level in t: Edit Level opens the selected level in the editor. We will use it in a moment.
strings.The Editor button at the bottom opens th: The Editor button at the bottom opens the level editor with a new, empty level, without picking one here first.
strings.Locations group levels together, like Do: Locations group levels together, like Downtown or Construction. Each has its own levels and settings, and you can add or reorder them here.
strings.Textures are the pictures your levels ar: Textures are the pictures your levels are made of. Browse the project's textures here, or import your own.
strings.Animations holds the moves file and the: Animations holds the moves file and the animation files of the characters' moves. Select one to preview it on the character.
strings.Tricks are the special moves players buy: Tricks are the special moves players buy in the shop and perform in levels. Here you set their names, icons and prices.
strings.Gears are the items players buy in the s: Gears are the items players buy in the shop. Here too you set their names, icons and prices.
strings.Models are the files of the game's chara: Models are the files of the game's characters, such as the runner and the hunter.
Music is the songs your levels can play.
Sounds are the game's sound effects.
strings.Videos are the cutscenes that can play a: Videos are the cutscenes that can play at the start or the end of a level.
XML Files are the project's data files. Vectorier writes them for you, so you rarely need to open them yourself.
strings.That's every category. Now click Levels: That's every category. Now click Levels to go back.
strings.Time to make a level of your own. Click: Time to make a level of your own. Click New Level (the + button) to add one to Downtown.
strings.Your new level {0} is selected. Click Ed: Your new level {0} is selected. Click Edit Level to open it in the editor.
strings.Welcome to the Level Editor, where you b: Welcome to the Level Editor, where you build levels. Let's have a quick look around first.
strings.The top menu has every command: File (sa: The top menu has every command: File (save, play, Level Settings), Edit (undo, copy, delete...), Element (add things to the level) and Help.
strings.The toolbar holds the tools that move, r: The toolbar holds the tools that move, rotate and resize things, plus Undo, Save, Level Settings and the way back to the Project Manager.
strings.The Element Bar lists everything you can: The Element Bar lists everything you can put in a level: images, platforms, objects, triggers, spawns and more. Click one to start placing it. The eye next to it shows or hides that kind in the Scene.
strings.The Hierarchy lists everything in the le: The Hierarchy lists everything in the level as a tree. Click a name to select it.
strings.The Project window shows what you can pl: The Project window shows what you can place for the chosen element: textures for images, objects, platforms and so on.
strings.The Inspector shows the settings of the: The Inspector shows the settings of the selected element: its position, size, layer and more.
strings.And in the middle is the Scene: your lev: And in the middle is the Scene: your level. Drag with the right mouse button to look around, and use the mouse wheel to zoom.
strings.Every level needs a place where the runn: Every level needs a place where the runner starts. Click Spawn in the Element Bar.
strings.Now click anywhere in the Scene to place: Now click anywhere in the Scene to place it.
strings.This is the spawn point: where the runne: This is the spawn point: where the runner appears when the level starts.
strings.Click the spawn in the Scene (or its nam: Click the spawn in the Scene (or its name in the Hierarchy) to select it.
strings.With a spawn selected, the Inspector has: With a spawn selected, the Inspector has a Preview Animation button. Click it.
strings.The runner appears at the spawn and play: The runner appears at the spawn and plays its starting move, so you can see where it will go. The Move Visualizer on the right can play any move anywhere in the level, to check jumps and distances while you build.
Click the Inspector tab to go back.
strings.Next, the camera. Click Camera in the El: Next, the camera. Click Camera in the Element Bar.
strings.Click in the Scene, near the spawn, to p: Click in the Scene, near the spawn, to place the camera.
strings.The camera decides what the player sees: The camera decides what the player sees at the start. Click the Game tab to look through it.
strings.This is what the camera sees, like the g: This is what the camera sees, like the game would show it. The Game view is only for looking: you build in the Scene.
Click the Scene tab to go back.
Let's give the level a background.
Images are pictures placed in the level. Click Images in the Element Bar.
strings.The Project window now shows the texture: The Project window now shows the textures (we hid all but one for now). Click v_bg.
strings.Click in the Scene to place it. The see-: Click in the Scene to place it. The see-through picture under the pointer shows where it will go.
strings.Something far away should move slower th: Something far away should move slower than the ground when the runner runs past. Layers do that. In the Inspector, set Layer to Background.
strings.The background is now on the Background: The background is now on the Background layer, so it scrolls slowly in the game. We also moved it to -1000, 500, so it sits behind the start of the level.
strings.The runner has nowhere to stand! Let's a: The runner has nowhere to stand! Let's add a platform: the ground it runs on.
Click Platform in the Element Bar.
strings.The Project window shows three platform: The Project window shows three platform styles: rough, smooth and block. Click rough.
strings.Click in the Scene to place it, or drag: Click in the Scene to place it, or drag to draw its size.
strings.Tools change what dragging does. Pick th: Tools change what dragging does. Pick the Move tool in the toolbar (or press Q).
strings.Drag the platform, or one of its arrows,: Drag the platform, or one of its arrows, to move it. Let go when you're done.
Now pick the Scale tool (or press E).
strings.Drag one of the handles to stretch the p: Drag one of the handles to stretch the platform.
strings.Last one: pick the Rect tool (or press T: Last one: pick the Rect tool (or press T).
strings.Drag an edge or a corner to resize the p: Drag an edge or a corner to resize the platform.
strings.The runner needs room. Make the platform: The runner needs room. Make the platform 2000 wide and 500 high: drag its edges (it stops growing at that size), or type the size in the Inspector.
strings.Your level can be played now. You can st: Your level can be played now. You can still move things around in the Scene: put the spawn just above the platform so the runner lands on it. When you're ready, click Play, and close the game when you're done.
strings.Running is nice, but let's add something: Running is nice, but let's add something to jump over.
strings.Objects are ready-made pieces: obstacles: Objects are ready-made pieces: obstacles, buildings, props. Click Objects in the Element Bar.
strings.Objects are stored in XML files, listed: Objects are stored in XML files, listed on the left. On the right are the objects of the chosen file. Click SmallPipeT.
strings.Click in the Scene to place it, somewher: Click in the Scene to place it, somewhere above the platform.
strings.Snapping puts things exactly on a platfo: Snapping puts things exactly on a platform. Point at the obstacle in the Scene and hold C: its corners light up. Grab its bottom corner and drag it onto the top of the platform, then let go.
strings.Move the obstacle wherever you like on t: Move the obstacle wherever you like on the platform. Click Next when you're happy with it.
strings.Play the level and jump over the obstacl: Play the level and jump over the obstacle with the Up key. Close the game when you're done.
strings.Items are things the runner collects. Cl: Items are things the runner collects. Click Item in the Element Bar.
Click Bonus in the Project window.
Click in the Scene to place it.
strings.Move the bonus anywhere the runner will: Move the bonus anywhere the runner will pass, for example just above the obstacle. Click Next when you're done.
strings.Play the level and grab the bonus. Close: Play the level and grab the bonus. Close the game when you're done.
strings.Did you notice? The camera stays where y: Did you notice? The camera stays where you put it instead of following the runner. A trigger can fix that: a zone that does something when the runner touches it.
Click Trigger in the Element Bar.
strings.Drag in the Scene to draw the trigger wh: Drag in the Scene to draw the trigger where the runner passes, for example over the spawn.
strings.Give the trigger a name in the Inspector: Give the trigger a name in the Inspector (any name will do), then press Enter.
strings.What a trigger does is set in the Trigge: What a trigger does is set in the Trigger Editor. Click Open Trigger Editor.
strings.At the top: Apply writes your changes in: At the top: Apply writes your changes into the trigger. Presets and Edit Templates let you reuse ready-made triggers.
strings.A trigger is made of loops. Each loop wa: A trigger is made of loops. Each loop waits for something to happen, checks its conditions, then does its actions.
strings.Variables are values the trigger reads a: Variables are values the trigger reads and changes. AI decides who can set it off: anyone, only the player or only the hunter.
strings.The right side edits the selected loop:: The right side edits the selected loop: When (the events it waits for), Only If (its conditions) and Do (its actions).
strings.Under When, click Add Event and choose M: Under When, click Add Event and choose Model Enters the Trigger.
strings.Under Do, click Add Action and choose Ca: Under Do, click Add Action and choose Camera › Follow Model.
strings.In Variables, set AI to Player, so only: In Variables, set AI to Player, so only the runner sets it off (and not the hunter).
Click Apply to save the trigger.
strings.Close the Trigger Editor with the X at t: Close the Trigger Editor with the X at the top right.
strings.Play the level: once the runner runs int: Play the level: once the runner runs into the trigger, the camera follows it. Close the game when you're done.
Last, a few settings of the whole level. Click Level Settings in the toolbar.
strings.Level Settings holds what belongs to the: Level Settings holds what belongs to the whole level: its thumbnail, music, coins and characters.
strings.Pick the music your level plays here, an: Pick the music your level plays here, and listen to it with the play button. Change it whenever you like.
strings.These are the characters of the level. E: These are the characters of the level. Each has a Name, a Type, a Color, a Birth Spawn (the spawn it starts at), an AI (who controls it: the player or the computer) and a Time (how long it waits before it starts running). Skins change how it looks.
Go back to the General tab.
strings.Every level has a thumbnail, shown when: Every level has a thumbnail, shown when picking levels. Click Capture from Scene…
strings.Move and zoom the view to frame your lev: Move and zoom the view to frame your level nicely, then click Apply.
Click Apply to close Level Settings.
strings.Finally, save your level: open the File: Finally, save your level: open the File menu and choose Save (or press Ctrl+S).
strings.Well done! You created a project and a l:
Well done! You created a project and a level with a spawn, a camera, a background, a platform, an obstacle, a bonus and a trigger, played it, and saved it.

From here, try other objects and textures, use triggers to make things happen, and check your jumps with the Move Visualizer. Help › Keybinds lists every shortcut, and Help › Tutorial plays this tutorial again.

Have fun building!
strings.Leave the tutorial? You can start it aga: Leave the tutorial? You can start it again any time from Help › Tutorial in the editor.
strings.The game is running.\nClose the game win:
The game is running.
Close the game window to continue the tutorial.
strings.Vectorier is a community-developed level: Vectorier is a community-developed level editor for the game Vector, where you build your own dystopian stages full of rooftops, obstacles and daring escapes.
strings.Before you get into modding Vector, it i: Before you get into modding Vector, it is worth learning how the editor works. This short tutorial walks you through creating a project and building your first playable level, one step at a time.
strings.You can leave the tutorial at any time,: You can leave the tutorial at any time, and start it again later from Help › Tutorial in the editor.
